scope: Theorem 8.6 (The marked-increment working package) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 69. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let C be a working scheme with com- ponentwise arrows and a stationary finite prescription as in Definition 8.1. Assume the eligible- subclass hypothesis of Convention 5.3. On an unbounded further class of sufficiently closed eligible levels, Cb is again a working scheme, with componentwise arrows, fixed template Fb, and mixed arrows between these levels. The output class retains the eligible-subclass hypothesis. The added language and bound recipes at this step have set-sized bounds in the input template and prescription. Thus the construction can be performed at each fixed finite depth without class-sized parameters or a language size depending on the level.
